title: Episode 2: The Fruit of the Tree

ending.reason: Sauti's story in brief closes on the war ("...he made the Kshatriyas kill each other in the terrific war that ensued."). It is a narration boundary; ¶30 turns to Dhritarashtra's lament (Episode 3).

segments.label: The fruit of the tree: the story in brief
segments.note: Vyasa fathers the three princes; how the Bharata was compiled and handed down; Pandu's misfortune and the birth of the Pandavas; their welcome at Hastinapura; Draupadi; Indraprastha, the Rajasuya and Duryodhana's envy; the dice and the war.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Sauti continued,
lines.tts_text: Sauti continued,

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: I will now speak of the undying flowery and fruitful productions of this tree, possessed of pure and pleasant taste, and not to be destroyed even by the immortals.
lines.tts_text: I will now speak of the undying flowery and fruitful productions of this tree, possessed of pure and pleasant taste, and not to be destroyed even by the immortals.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Formerly, the spirited and virtuous Krishna-Dwaipayana, by the injunctions of Bhishma, the wise son of Ganga and of his own mother, became the father of three boys who were like the three fires by the two wives of Vichitra-virya; and having thus raised up Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura, he returned to his recluse abode to prosecute his religious exercise.
lines.tts_text: Formerly, the spirited and virtuous Krishna Dwaipayana, by the injunctions of Bhishma, the wise son of Ganga and of his own mother, became the father of three boys who were like the three fires by the two wives of Vichitra-virya; and having thus raised up Dhritarashtra, Pandu and Vidura, he returned to his recluse abode to prosecute his religious exercise.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: It was not till after these were born, grown up, and departed on the supreme journey, that the great Rishi Vyasa published the Bharata in this region of mankind; when being solicited by Janamejaya and thousands of Brahmanas, he instructed his disciple Vaisampayana, who was seated near him; and he, sitting together with the Sadasyas, recited the Bharata, during the intervals of the ceremonies of the sacrifice, being repeatedly urged to proceed.
lines.tts_text: It was not till after these were born, grown up, and departed on the supreme journey, that the great Rishee Vyasa published the Bharata in this region of mankind; when being solicited by Janamejaya and thousands of Brahmanas, he instructed his disciple Vaisampayana, who was seated near him; and he, sitting together with the Sadasyas, recited the Bharata, during the intervals of the ceremonies of the sacrifice, being repeatedly urged to proceed.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Vyasa hath fully represented the greatness of the house of Kuru, the virtuous principles of Gandhari, the wisdom of Vidura, and the constancy of Kunti.
lines.tts_text: Vyasa hath fully represented the greatness of the house of Kuru, the virtuous principles of Gandhari, the wisdom of Vidura, and the constancy of Kunti.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The noble Rishi hath also described the divinity of Vasudeva, the rectitude of the sons of Pandu, and the evil practices of the sons and partisans of Dhritarashtra.
lines.tts_text: The noble Rishee hath also described the divinity of Vasudeva, the rectitude of the sons of Pandu, and the evil practices of the sons and partisans of Dhritarashtra.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Vyasa executed the compilation of the Bharata, exclusive of the episodes originally in twenty-four thousand verses; and so much only is called by the learned as the Bharata.
lines.tts_text: Vyasa executed the compilation of the Bharata, exclusive of the episodes originally in twenty-four thousand verses; and so much only is called by the learned as the Bharata.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Afterwards, he composed an epitome in one hundred and fifty verses, consisting of the introduction with the chapter of contents.
lines.tts_text: Afterwards, he composed an epitome in one hundred and fifty verses, consisting of the introduction with the chapter of contents.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: This he first taught to his son Suka; and afterwards he gave it to others of his disciples who were possessed of the same qualifications.
lines.tts_text: This he first taught to his son Suka; and afterwards he gave it to others of his disciples who were possessed of the same qualifications.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After that he executed another compilation, consisting of six hundred thousand verses.
lines.tts_text: After that he executed another compilation, consisting of six hundred thousand verses.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Of those, thirty hundred thousand are known in the world of the Devas; fifteen hundred thousand in the world of the Pitris: fourteen hundred thousand among the Gandharvas, and one hundred thousand in the regions of mankind.
lines.tts_text: Of those, thirty hundred thousand are known in the world of the Devas; fifteen hundred thousand in the world of the Pitris: fourteen hundred thousand among the Gandharvas, and one hundred thousand in the regions of mankind.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Narada recited them to the Devas, Devala to the Pitris, and Suka published them to the Gandharvas, Yakshas, and Rakshasas: and in this world they were recited by Vaisampayana, one of the disciples of Vyasa, a man of just principles and the first among all those acquainted with the Vedas.
lines.tts_text: Naaruda recited them to the Devas, Devala to the Pitris, and Suka published them to the Gandharvas, Yakshas, and Rakshasas: and in this world they were recited by Vaisampayana, one of the disciples of Vyasa, a man of just principles and the first among all those acquainted with the Vedas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Know that I, Sauti, have also repeated one hundred thousand verses.
lines.tts_text: Know that I, Sauti, have also repeated one hundred thousand verses.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Yudhishthira is a vast tree, formed of religion and virtue; Arjuna is its trunk; Bhimasena, its branches; the two sons of Madri are its full-grown fruit and flowers; and its roots are Krishna, Brahma, and the Brahmanas.
lines.tts_text: Yudhishthira is a vast tree, formed of religion and virtue; Arjoona is its trunk; Bhimasena, its branches; the two sons of Madri are its full-grown fruit and flowers; and its roots are Krishna, Brahma, and the Brahmanas.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Pandu, after having subdued many countries by his wisdom and prowess, took up his abode with the Munis in a certain forest as a sportsman, where he brought upon himself a very severe misfortune for having killed a stag coupling with its mate, which served as a warning for the conduct of the princes of his house as long as they lived.
lines.tts_text: Pandu, after having subdued many countries by his wisdom and prowess, took up his abode with the Moonees in a certain forest as a sportsman, where he brought upon himself a very severe misfortune for having killed a stag coupling with its mate, which served as a warning for the conduct of the princes of his house as long as they lived.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Their mothers, in order that the ordinances of the law might be fulfilled, admitted as substitutes to their embraces the gods Dharma, Vayu, Sakra, and the divinities the twin Aswins.
lines.tts_text: Their mothers, in order that the ordinances of the law might be fulfilled, admitted as substitutes to their embraces the gods Dharma, Vayu, Shakra, and the divinities the twin Aswins.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And when their offspring grew up, under the care of their two mothers, in the society of ascetics, in the midst of sacred groves and holy recluse-abodes of religious men, they were conducted by Rishis into the presence of Dhritarashtra and his sons, following as students in the habit of Brahmacharis, having their hair tied in knots on their heads.
lines.tts_text: And when their offspring grew up, under the care of their two mothers, in the society of ascetics, in the midst of sacred groves and holy recluse-abodes of religious men, they were conducted by Rishis into the presence of Dhritarashtra and his sons, following as students in the habit of Brahmachaarees, having their hair tied in knots on their heads.

lines.speaker: satasringa_rishis
lines.text: 'These our pupils',
lines.tts_text: 'These our pupils',
lines.direction: the forest sages presenting their pupils to the Kuru court, gentle and grave

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: said they,
lines.tts_text: said they,

lines.speaker: satasringa_rishis
lines.text: 'are as your sons, your brothers, and your friends; they are Pandavas.'
lines.tts_text: 'are as your sons, your brothers, and your friends; they are Pandavas.'
lines.direction: a blessing and a charge to the court

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Saying this, the Munis disappeared.
lines.tts_text: Saying this, the Moonees disappeared.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: When the Kauravas saw them introduced as the sons of Pandu, the distinguished class of citizens shouted exceedingly for joy.
lines.tts_text: When the Kauravas saw them introduced as the sons of Pandu, the distinguished class of citizens shouted exceedingly for joy.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Some, however, said, they were not the sons of Pandu; others said, they were; while a few asked how they could be his offspring, seeing he had been so long dead.
lines.tts_text: Some, however, said, they were not the sons of Pandu; others said, they were; while a few asked how they could be his offspring, seeing he had been so long dead.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Still on all sides voices were heard crying,
lines.tts_text: Still on all sides voices were heard crying,

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: They are on all accounts welcome!
lines.tts_text: They are on all accounts welcome!
lines.direction: the citizens' joyful cry, voiced by the narrator (no crowd voice yet)

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Through divine Providence we behold the family of Pandu!
lines.tts_text: Through divine Providence we behold the family of Pandu!
lines.direction: the citizens' joyful cry, voiced by the narrator (no crowd voice yet)

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Let their welcome be proclaimed!
lines.tts_text: Let their welcome be proclaimed!
lines.direction: the citizens' joyful cry, voiced by the narrator (no crowd voice yet)

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: As these acclamations ceased, the plaudits of invisible spirits, causing every point of the heavens to resound, were tremendous.
lines.tts_text: As these acclamations ceased, the plaudits of invisible spirits, causing every point of the heavens to resound, were tremendous.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: There were showers of sweet-scented flowers, and the sound of shells and kettle-drums.
lines.tts_text: There were showers of sweet-scented flowers, and the sound of shells and kettle-drums.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Such were the wonders that happened on the arrival of the young princes.
lines.tts_text: Such were the wonders that happened on the arrival of the young princes.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The joyful noise of all the citizens, in expression of their satisfaction on the occasion, was so great that it reached the very heavens in magnifying plaudits.
lines.tts_text: The joyful noise of all the citizens, in expression of their satisfaction on the occasion, was so great that it reached the very heavens in magnifying plaudits.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Having studied the whole of the Vedas and sundry other shastras, the Pandavas resided there, respected by all and without apprehension from any one.
lines.tts_text: Having studied the whole of the Vedas and sundry other Shastras, the Pandavas resided there, respected by all and without apprehension from any one.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The principal men were pleased with the purity of Yudhishthira, the courage of Arjuna, the submissive attention of Kunti to her superiors, and the humility of the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva; and all the people rejoiced in their heroic virtues.
lines.tts_text: The principal men were pleased with the purity of Yudhishthira, the courage of Arjoona, the submissive attention of Kunti to her superiors, and the humility of the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva; and all the people rejoiced in their heroic virtues.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: After a while, Arjuna obtained the virgin Krishna at the swayamvara, in the midst of a concourse of Rajas, by performing a very difficult feat of archery.
lines.tts_text: After a while, Arjoona obtained the virgin Drowpadee at the swayamvara, in the midst of a concourse of Rajas, by performing a very difficult feat of archery.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And from this time he became very much respected in this world among all bowmen; and in fields of battle also, like the sun, he was hard to behold by foe-men.
lines.tts_text: And from this time he became very much respected in this world among all bowmen; and in fields of battle also, like the sun, he was hard to behold by foe-men.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And having vanquished all the neighbouring princes and every considerable tribe, he accomplished all that was necessary for the Raja (his eldest brother) to perform the great sacrifice called Rajasuya.
lines.tts_text: And having vanquished all the neighbouring princes and every considerable tribe, he accomplished all that was necessary for the Raja to perform the great sacrifice called Rajasuya.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Yudhishthira, after having, through the wise counsels of Vasudeva and by the valour of Bhimasena and Arjuna, slain Jarasandha (the king of Magadha) and the proud Chaidya, acquired the right to perform the grand sacrifice of Rajasuya abounding in provisions and offering and fraught with transcendent merits.
lines.tts_text: Yudhishthira, after having, through the wise counsels of Vasudeva and by the valour of Bhimasena and Arjoona, slain Jarasandha and the proud Chaidya, acquired the right to perform the grand sacrifice of Rajasuya abounding in provisions and offering and fraught with transcendent merits.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And Duryodhana came to this sacrifice; and when he beheld the vast wealth of the Pandavas scattered all around, the offerings, the precious stones, gold and jewels; the wealth in cows, elephants, and horses; the curious textures, garments, and mantles; the precious shawls and furs and carpets made of the skin of the Ranku; he was filled with envy and became exceedingly displeased.
lines.tts_text: And Duryodhana came to this sacrifice; and when he beheld the vast wealth of the Pandavas scattered all around, the offerings, the precious stones, gold and jewels; the wealth in cows, elephants, and horses; the curious textures, garments, and mantles; the precious shawls and furs and carpets made of the skin of the Ranku; he was filled with envy and became exceedingly displeased.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And when he beheld the hall of assembly elegantly constructed by Maya (the Asura architect) after the fashion of a celestial court, he was inflamed with rage.
lines.tts_text: And when he beheld the hall of assembly elegantly constructed by Maya after the fashion of a celestial court, he was inflamed with rage.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And having started in confusion at certain architectural deceptions within this building, he was derided by Bhimasena in the presence of Vasudeva, like one of mean descent.
lines.tts_text: And having started in confusion at certain architectural deceptions within this building, he was derided by Bhimasena in the presence of Vasudeva, like one of mean descent.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And it was represented to Dhritarashtra that his son, while partaking of various objects of enjoyment and diverse precious things, was becoming meagre, wan, and pale.
lines.tts_text: And it was represented to Dhritarashtra that his son, while partaking of various objects of enjoyment and diverse precious things, was becoming meagre, wan, and pale.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And Dhritarashtra, some time after, out of affection for his son, gave his consent to their playing (with the Pandavas) at dice.
lines.tts_text: And Dhritarashtra, some time after, out of affection for his son, gave his consent to their playing at dice.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And Vasudeva coming to know of this, became exceedingly wroth.
lines.tts_text: And Vasudeva coming to know of this, became exceedingly wroth.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: And being dissatisfied, he did nothing to prevent the disputes, but overlooked the gaming and sundry other horried unjustifiable transactions arising therefrom: and in spite of Vidura, Bhishma, Drona, and Kripa, the son of Saradwan, he made the Kshatriyas kill each other in the terrific war that ensued.'
lines.tts_text: And being dissatisfied, he did nothing to prevent the disputes, but overlooked the gaming and sundry other horrid unjustifiable transactions arising therefrom: and in spite of Vidura, Bhishma, Drona, and Kripaa, the son of Saradwan, he made the Kshatriyas kill each other in the terrific war that ensued.'
lines.direction: the shadow of the war falls; end of the story in brief
